title: Proof Conductor: cross-border evidence orchestration & audit pack automation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: build a reusable orchestration layer (Proof Conductor) that assembles, signs, and exports audit-ready evidence bundles for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 audits across regional data residency constraints. The conductor will: 1) map runtime and infra telemetry to control assertions (e.g., access reviews, retention events, key management actions), 2) collect artifacts from multiple sources (runtime logs, KV cache eviction traces, retention policy change events, object store manifests), 3) enforce jurisdictional residency rules during export and packaging, and 4) generate a tamper-evident audit pack optionally signed with customer-bound KMS keys. This ticket owns the PM scope, acceptance criteria, rollout strategy, and cross-team coordination with Eng (collectors + signer), Security (KMS and proof model), and Console (export UI + license/consent flows).
background: Customers with regulated workloads (finance, healthcare, government) require fast, reproducible evidence for controls that span hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Current evidence assembly is manual, scattered across dashboards, object stores, and infra alerts, causing long audit cycles. Proof Conductor aims to reduce audit prep time by automating mapping/collection and ensuring exported artifacts respect residency and retention constraints.
out_of_scope: Long-term archival storage tiering for 10+ year retention (this will be a follow-up). Deep legal export approvals; we provide policy knobs and provenance, not legal authorization workflows.
approach_summary: We will implement a two-phase rollout: Phase 1 (internal beta) - orchestration that collects and bundles evidence for Redwood-managed hosted accounts, using a Redwood signing key and region-aware packaging. Phase 2 (enterprise release) - allow customer-supplied signing via KMS, VPC-aware collectors for Private deployments, and per-customer export policies that redact or exclude jurisdictionally restricted artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Control mapping: each SOC 2 CC/ISO A.x control targeted by the playbook has a documented mapping to at least one telemetry source and collection hook
Collector coverage: eng collectors can surface access logs, retention policy change events, object manifests, and runtime KV cache snapshots for >90% of sample test scenarios
Residency enforcement: evidence export flow honors per-customer region allowlist/denylist and blocks artifacts originating from denied regions
Audit pack: system can produce a downloadable audit bundle (manifest + artifacts + signing metadata) that passes a tamper check and includes a control-to-artifact index
KMS signing: enterprise customers can opt-in to sign bundles with a customer KMS key (SaaS-managed or customer-managed HSM)
Console UX: export request with residency validation and a progress indicator is available in Console for enterprise customers
Performance: typical 1GB audit bundle generation completes under 120s for hosted demo tenant (excluding slow object store reads)
Security review: security team sign-off on threat model, signing model, and key handling
tasks: Write control-to-telemetry mapping doc (PM + Security) - link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/ProofConductorMapping
Design collector contracts (ENG) - define schemas and backfill requirements
Prototype evidence packaging format (manifest.json + artifact index + signatures) - eng prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proof-conductor/pull/72
Implement residency filter middleware in export service (ENG-18421)
Console export UX + admin policy page (Product + Design)
Create test-suite of audit scenarios covering hosted/dedicated/private deployments
Documentation: admin playbook and auditor guide for produced bundles
risks: Residency enforcement depends on accurate artifact origin metadata — if upstream services do not reliably tag region, exports might leak. Signing model complexity increases for private deployments that cannot reach our KMS; we must support customer-supplied keys. Large bundles may time out depending on object store throughput; consider streaming pack creation.
tradeoffs: We could build a minimal PoC that only bundles Console logs (fast), but that won't satisfy enterprise auditors. Alternative is to require manual attestations for certain private artifacts which slows audit turnaround. We prioritize automated coverage for hosted + Dedicated first.
